overview.description: 98: adding game. Play one card to a central pile and announce new total. A-9 add face value; 10 subtracts 10; J/Q no change; K sets pile to 98. Avoid exceeding 98; first to push total over 98 loses. Often played as drinking game.

history.origins: Adding game; likely North American mid-20th century. Families reported playing 98 in the 1970s, 99 in the 1950s. Similar to 99 and 100 (same family).
timeline: Mid 20th century: adding games 98, 99, and 100 emerge in North America, with families reporting play in the 1950s and 1970s.
1993: Arizona State University players create a more complex 98 variant with jokers and additional special cards that spreads to other colleges.
history.cultural: USA; often played as drinking game.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

rules.objective: Avoid being the player who pushes the central total over 98.
rules.gameplay: Play one card per turn; add (A-9), subtract (10), hold (J/Q), or set to 98 (K). Announce new total; over 98 = lose.
keyRules: A-9 add face value; 10 subtracts 10; J/Q no change; K sets to 98

strategy.basic: Save K for 98 reset; use 10 to lower total when high.
strategy.intermediate: Track running total; force opponents near 98.
strategy.advanced: Card counting; when to push vs hold.
tips: K = reset to 98; 10 = -10; avoid going over.

list.name: UMass Amherst variant
list.description: Extra special cards: Ace of Clubs/Diamonds +1 or +11; Ace of Spades pick player to eliminate; Ace of Hearts blocks Spades and discard/draw; Four reverses direction; Nine counts zero and pass turn; Ten +10 or -10; King sets to 98; Queen of Spades exchange hands; other Queens and all Jacks +10.
list.emptyOverridesReason: This variation is described only in rules text; specific engine overrides have not yet been modeled.

list.name: 98 Arizona version
list.description: Standard 52-card pack with two jokers. Four cards each; play to center pile. Ace +1 or +11; Nine reverses direction; Jack -10; Queen or Four zero; King sets to 98; Joker sets to 98 and next player must play twice on 98 or play other joker. Multiple cards of same rank may be played together (total value added); draw that many to refill. When stock runs out, play continues without replenishment until one player remains.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Arizona version is documented narratively; engine-level overrides for this variant are not yet captured.
